links.outcome: Effect of an automated code verification step on LLM clinical coding accuracy
links.effect: Verification is reported as an effective and reliable step for improving LLM-based medical coding, addressing hierarchically near-miss errors. No numbers are given in the abstract.
links.quote: Our results highlight verification as an effective and reliable step toward improving LLM-based medical coding.

unlisted_practices: Lightweight prompt engineering and small-scale fine-tuning to improve LLM clinical coding accuracy
Hierarchy-aware error analysis of near-miss ICD-10 code predictions instead of exact-match metrics
Expert double-annotated outpatient benchmark to correct inpatient bias in MIMIC

screen.practice: LLM-based code verification step, prompt engineering, and lightweight fine-tuning
screen.reason: The study evaluates lightweight guardrail/pipeline practices, specifically automated post-generation clinical code verification and prompt interventions, to catch and mitigate hierarchical miscoding errors in LLMs.
